hardened.config: Codemode.create({ timeoutMs: 5000, memoryLimitBytes: 16 MiB, maxRunsPerWorker: 1, outputLimit: { lines: 3, bytes: 1024 }, outputDir }) per docs/sdk.md 'Instance lifecycle' and 'Limit a run's result' (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/docs/sdk.md). 8 MiB is the engine floor but no worker starts below 12 MiB (out/hardened-min-memory.txt). defaults.memory: 64 MiB V8 old generation per worker via resourceLimits (config/types.ts:51, engine.ts:413). Not reliable: 7 of 24 P7 runs aborted the whole host.
defaults.output: 2,000 lines and 50 KB per result, error and logs, keeping the last lines and naming a full-output file (utils/output-limit.ts:17-18).
defaults.tool_calls: No per-run cap found. Each action may hold 8 MiB of output (maxActionOutputBytes).

source_notes.finding: A worker_threads Worker inside the host process, created with eval: true, env: {} and resourceLimits. Bodies are compiled with new Function and receive require (a wrapper that only blanks worker_threads.parentPort) and the global process. The authors say plainly it is not a sandbox, and the code matches that.

env: {} empties process.env inside the worker, and the comment explains why (host secrets one line away). docs/security.md:17 says the worker keeps the host's environment away from calling code. P5 shows ps eww on the shared PID still prints the host env, so that claim does not hold once child_process is available.

Each plugin is a Proxy global; calling plugin.a.b(args) posts {t: 'invoke', path, args} to the host, which validates args against the action's TypeBox schema, resolves a connection, and runs execute(). Names are always plugin.action.

On demand, inside the program: actions.find(query, limit = 5) searches with the ferrosearch native index, actions.describe(path) returns one signature, actions.check(path, input) validates without calling. No schema dump in the prompt, so it scales past 100 tools.

Async postMessage over the worker's parentPort with an unguessable runId per run (randomUUID) so a body cannot forge a done message for another run. Calls return promises, so Promise.all overlaps them (P9).

ExecuteResult {result, error, logs}. result is the JSON of the returned value; console.* is bridged into logs. Each is cut to 2,000 lines / 50 KB keeping the last lines, with a marker naming a full-output file the host writes to outputDir.

Timeout via a host setTimeout that terminates the worker (#L453-L466). Memory via resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb on Node; an RSS watchdog arms only under Bun, which ignores resourceLimits (#L190-L198, #L469-L485). OOM surfaces as ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY when V8 terminates the worker cleanly (#L567), but V8 sometimes aborts the whole process instead (P7).

One pooled worker serves up to 500 runs (maxRunsPerWorker). After each run it deletes new globals and compares listed intrinsics; a leftover timer, undeletable global or touched intrinsic retires the worker. The process object is not checked, so state hung on it survives (P8). Concurrent execute() calls get throwaway workers.

Caught in the worker and formatted as message plus stack (__fmtErr); execute() never rejects. Line numbers are user line + 3. The output limit applies to the error too and keeps the last lines, so a tight limit drops the message and keeps the stack tail (hardened P3).

Actions run on the host with connections the guest cannot read via the bridge; an optional credentialBroker signs requests outside the plugin process and declared credentials are only sent to declared HTTPS targets. But the guest can read ~/.codemode or project config.json directly with require('fs'), which docs/security.md admits.
MIT license; pinned commit dated 2026-11-22; npm @shiftlabs/codemode 0.46.0 published 2026-11-21 from an older commit. Large bundled plugin set (200+ services).

surprises: The default 64 MB memory limit is not containment: 7 of 24 runs of the literal P7 code aborted the whole host process with a V8 fatal OOM instead of terminating the worker (6 of 12 with an extra distinct-string variant). The engine's own doc comment promises the opposite: 'crash containment: a dead worker never takes the host process down' (packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts:218).
docs/security.md:17 says the worker keeps the host's environment variables away from calling code. process.env is empty, but ps eww on the shared PID printed the host's PROBE_SECRET in one line.
fetch is 'disabled' only as a shadowed name: globalThis.fetch is Node's real fetch and reached example.com (200).
The pooled worker's state scrub misses the process object: a property set on process in one run is visible to the next run, which may belong to another caller.
The memory floor in code is 8 MB, but a worker cannot start below 12 MB; every run then fails with 'Memory limit exceeded'.
The npm 0.46.0 tarball (gitHead 96683925) predates the pinned commit by 73 changed files in packages/codemode/src, including the whole output-limit feature that docs/sdk.md now documents.
package.json keywords include "sandbox" and the fetch stub error says 'codemode sandbox', while the README and security doc say it is not a sandbox.
